candidates.name: Airbnb-Price-Analysis-in-Athens
candidates.what_it_holds: data/athens_weekdays.csv and data/athens_weekends.csv, split by weekday vs weekend pricing. Shape/variable naming (weekday/weekend price split for a single European city) matches the well-known Gyodi & Nawaro 'Determinants of Airbnb prices in European cities' academic dataset (originally covering Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, Paris, Rome, Vienna, London — ~5,000 listings/city, hedonic variables: room type, bedrooms, person capacity, superhost flag, cleanliness/guest satisfaction ratings, distance to center, restaurant/attraction indices). Repo itself is a small student analysis but the committed CSVs appear to be that dataset (or a close re-derivation) landing on GitHub, which we do not currently hold.
candidates.why_useful: If this is (or reproduces) the Gyodi-Nawaro weekday/weekend European hedonic panel, it directly fills our hedonic/mix-decomposition gap with a multi-city academic dataset that separately identifies bedroom/quality/superhost premia and a weekday-vs-weekend price wedge -- useful for ADR mix decomposition (gap 2/20) in EMEA markets outside our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.size_hint: 2 CSVs, likely ~5-6k rows total for Athens
candidates.time_coverage: unclear, likely a single 2018-era snapshot (matches original Gyodi/Nawaro data vintage)

candidates.name: airbnb_hedonic_pricing
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs: a listings file enriched with distance-to-nearest-subway-station (geocoded) and pororo_scoring.csv (Korean NLP sentiment scores computed over listing reviews). Hedonic feature set includes guest capacity, bed count, bathrooms, average rating, review volume, superhost status, ID verification, host response rate, deposit/cleaning fee, security camera, washer, free parking, photo count, plus the review-sentiment score and subway distance as location/quality proxies.
candidates.why_useful: A working example of turning review text into a quantitative listing-quality feature (sentiment score) combined with a hedonic regression -- directly relevant methodology for isolating a 'listing quality' or superhost premium net of location, which our mix-decomposition / ADR work needs a comparable technique for, even though the city (Seoul) is not one we track.
candidates.size_hint: small, single-city snapshot, unknown row count, 0 stars
candidates.time_coverage: unknown, appears to be a single scrape (repo last updated Dec 2022)
